rows: A build automation and project management tool primarily for Java. It uses an XML file (pom.xml) to configure dependencies, lifecycle, and plugins.
A file (e.g., JAR, WAR, EAR) generated during the Maven build process.
The Project Object Model file. It is the central configuration file in a Maven project that defines dependencies, plugins, goals, and project metadata.
Uniquely identifies a project across all Maven projects. It typically follows a reversed domain format (e.g., com.example.app).
The name of the specific project/module. It is typically unique within the group and becomes part of the generated artifact name.
Specifies the version of the artifact. Example versions include 1.0.0, 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.
A special version tag in Maven used during development. Indicates the artifact is still under active development and may change frequently.

items:
Standard Directory Structure (highly recommended): └── src
    ├── main
    │   ├── java
    │   └── resources
    └── test
        ├── java
        └── resources
└── target
✅ Store all generated artifacts (e.g., JAR, WAR, compiled classes) in the target folder. This helps in keeping your source tree clean and consistent.
✅ Use lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens () only for groupId and artifactId.
✅ Use ${project.artifactId} for project reference instead of hardcoding values. It improves maintainability and consistency.
✅ Use SNAPSHOT versions only during development.
✅ Group dependencies logically using Maven properties for shared versioning.
✅ Clearly define all repository references in pom.xml to ensure dependencies can be fetched properly.
✅ Use settings.xml to define mirrors if you want to fetch artifacts from a local repository rather than the internet:
✅ In multi-module projects, use dependency management in the parent pom.xml:
This avoids repeating version numbers in every child module.
❌ Avoid writing custom Maven plugin goals (like for file copy or unzip) when standard Maven plugins already exist.
